messages.subject: partial melt
parts:
Hi there
 
I have a pretty big dataframe (50'000 rows, 1'001 columns) in a weired wide format (originating Excel):
 
> head(dd)
     id  V1000 V1001  V1010 V1011 ...  V5990 V5991
1 83542 863X10     9   8363     3 ...    286     9
2 23822   <NA>    10 939699     5 ... 838836     4
3 51988 814519     7 815199     4 ... 381810     7
4 71130 991099     7 397113     9 ... 889411     3
5 38377   4575     3    741     7 ... 815199     2
6 15410   1341     5    897     3 ... 395011    10
 
What I need is a partial long format, like this:
 
> head(dr)
      id  V0000 V0001
1  83542 863X10     9
2  83542   8363     3
3  83542    286     9
4  23822   <NA>    10
5  23822 939699     5
6  23822 838836     4
7  51988 814519     7
8  51988 815199     4
9  51988 381810     7
10 71130 991099     7
 
Is there a possibility to "group" specific variables in the melt function?
Of course I could melt down the dataframe to "id", do some variable transformations and then expand it to the rigth level with dcast. But I'm on the edge of memory and every additional step brings me closre to "cannot allocate vector...".
 
Additionally: I found out, that melting the whole dataframe isn't possible because of memory-size. But melting subsets and binding them together works perfectly:
dr0=rbind(melt(dd[1:10000],, melt(dd[10001:20000,]), ... melt(dd[40001:50000,]))
 
Is there a possibility to include a "memory-save" param in the melt function for us poor 32-bit guys?
 
Thanks  -  Markus
